entries.name: Fixed destruction size
entries.description: Canonical fixed destruction size supplied by IteratedGreedyParameters.

entries.name: Stagnation-escalating destruction size
entries.description: Generic size escalation with a configurable stagnation window and cap. Inspired by adaptive-destruction IG research but not presented as an exact reproduction of a problem-specific AIG controller.
entries.publication: Adaptive-destruction design informed by Li et al. (2021)

entries.name: Partial-solution improvement hook
entries.description: Domain-defined improvement executed after destruction and before reconstruction. The common full-solution evaluator is deliberately not exposed.
entries.formula: A domain-defined operator improves the partial representation between destruction and reconstruction; partial objective semantics remain owned by the problem domain.

entries.name: Strict-improvement acceptance
entries.description: Accept only a strict improvement over the incumbent.

entries.name: Constant-temperature Metropolis acceptance
entries.description: Objective-scale Metropolis acceptance; problem-specific temperature normalization remains outside the generic core.

entries.name: Bounded-search Iterated Greedy
entries.description: Problem-structure-specific bounded search and multi-phase local improvement; not reducible to a generic destruction-size flag.
entries.formula: Distributed-flowshop-specific bounded search combines assignment/scheduling structure with dedicated local-search phases.

entries.name: Tabu-based reconstruction IG
entries.description: Tabu-based reconstruction plus dedicated insert/swap/double-insert local search.
entries.formula: The reconstruction phase uses Tabu memory and no-wait-flowshop-specific neighborhoods; an exact implementation requires dedicated reconstruction-memory semantics.

entries.name: IG with optimization of partial solutions
entries.description: The v0.38 partial-improvement hook supports faithful domain composition, but the exact PFSP partial local search remains problem-specific.
entries.formula: After destruction, a valid problem-specific partial objective is locally optimized before the removed components are reconstructed.

entries.name: Iterated Reference Greedy
entries.description: Reference-guided distributed no-idle mechanism requiring a first-class reference-solution contract.
entries.formula: A reference-guided greedy cycle uses problem-specific distributed no-idle structure; it is not equivalent to ordinary IG with a scalar parameter.

entries.name: Distributed PFSP Iterated Greedy methods
entries.description: Improved initialization, construction, destruction and strong intensification for distributed PFSP.
entries.formula: The published method couples factory assignment, specialized construction/destruction and distributed-flowshop local intensification.

entries.name: Best-of-breed Iterated Greedy
entries.description: Combined state-of-the-art PFSP mechanisms including FF insertion tie-breaking.
entries.formula: A specialized best-of-breed combination integrates PFSP acceleration and tie-breaking mechanisms rather than one generic control equation.

entries.name: Distributed PFSP due-windows Iterated Greedy
entries.formula: The method embeds distributed-flowshop due-window objective structure and dedicated operators that are not representation-independent.

entries.name: Adaptive Iterated Greedy
entries.description: Adaptive destruction sample length, restart, influence-based removal and problem-specific accelerations.
entries.formula: The exact AIG combines adaptive sample length, restart, influence-based removal, referenced local search and mixed-no-idle accelerations; v0.38 implements only representation-independent primitives.

entries.name: Two-stage Iterated Greedy
entries.description: Recent two-stage IG for distributed blocking flowshops.
entries.formula: The two-stage search is tied to blocking-flowshop structure and dedicated stage operators; it remains separately reviewed rather than being represented by a generic Boolean option.
